question: The magnetic field produced due to a circular coil carrying a current having six turns will be how many times that of the field produced due to a single circular loop carrying the same current?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 times**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **6 times** is the factor by which the magnetic field produced by a circular coil with six turns is greater than that produced by a single circular loop carrying the same current.
 
• The **magnetic field strength** (B) produced by a circular coil is **directly proportional to the number of turns** (N) in the coil.
 
• Hence, if a coil has 6 turns, the magnetic field strength will be 6 times that of a single loop.
 
• This relationship is given by the formula** B = (μ₀ * N * I) / (2 * R)**, where μ₀ is the permeability of free space, N is the number of turns, I is the current, and R is the radius of the coil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The relationship between the number of turns and the magnetic field strength is linear; doubling the number of turns doubles the magnetic field strength.
 
• This principle is utilized in electromagnets and inductors where multiple turns of wire are used to produce stronger magnetic fields.
 
• Understanding this principle is crucial in designing electrical devices that rely on magnetic fields.
 
• Factors such as the coil's radius and the current flowing through it also affect the magnetic field strength but were held constant in this scenario.
